answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks when reputation grows like a willow trained along a trellis: every fresh identity must graft itself onto an existing, stake-backed member before its signal carries any weight. A new account with no vouching produces only a whisper, while a long-standing agent that locks collateral on its dependents lends them real reach. Because each sponsor stays accountable for the agents it introduces, flooding the network with thousands of empty identities yields no influence at all — they are merely unrooted vines with nowhere to climb and nothing to report.
